messages:
maria: Heads up — during today's quantized eval runs I'm seeing trace payloads balloon to ~40-80MB per sample (mostly kv_cache + logits). S3 uploads start failing with 413 and the runner retries just pile up. Any quick mitigation ideas?

alex: ugh that size is wild. are these the full-token traces? can we drop the kv cache or gzip them before upload? CI multipart should handle >5MB but 413 implies request body too large not S3 part size.

maria: they are per-sample full traces (prompt + token outputs + kv dump for replays). gzip helps but we still hit the proxy limit from the runner -> upload presigned URL in some regions. also noticed some traces include raw user text with PII. need to avoid storing sensitive fields.

ryan: can we stream the trace directly to S3 instead of buffering in memory? runner currently builds payload then PUTs. streaming upload would avoid the 413 from proxy layer. also add a `x-trace-checksum` header so retries can dedupe.

alex: streaming is a good longer-term fix. short-term patch: 1) strip kv_cache from trace if quantization mode = "kv-trim" 2) add gzipped ndjson fallback 3) set per-run retention TTL to 7d for quantized-evals to limit storage blowup.

sophia: for PII we should run a light sanitizer that redacts known keys and masks free text with `--REDACTED--` when user_prompt_detected=true. we already have the redaction lib used by private-deployments. can we reuse it in runner? :thinking:

maria: yes reusing redaction lib (+a small allowlist) works. question: do we add `trace_schema_version` and `pii_redacted` flags to metadata? that'll help downstream dashboards and retention rules.

ryan: add both. also include `trace_size_bytes` and `upload_encoding` in the metadata to help cost accounting. small sample metadata format: 
```json
{
  "trace_schema_version": "v2.1",
  "pii_redacted": true,
  "trace_size_bytes": 45232123,
  "upload_encoding": "gzip+ndjson",
  "sample_seed": 12345
}
```

alex: FYI CI was throwing a different error earlier: the eval-runner uploaded a gzipped stream but content-encoding header wasn't set, so proxy rejected it. added a quick check in the upload code to set `Content-Encoding: gzip`. also added retry backoff so we don't clobber the proxy.

ci-bot: pipeline #4821 failed on step "eval-runner/integration" — artifact upload 413 -> retry exhausted (attempts=3). See https://ci.example/reports/4821

maria: OK actionable plan:
- (maria) wire redaction + `pii_redacted` metadata into runner (short patch)
- (alex) add `Content-Encoding` header + fallback ndjson multipart upload
- (ryan) prototype streaming PUT to presigned URL and add `x-trace-checksum`
- (sophia) write a small eval-cleaner job to sample heavy traces and keep only heads/tails for long conversations (configurable sample_rate)

Also let's add a retention config knob per-eval-suite in the artifact service (default 30d, override per-suite). that should prevent accidental long-term bloat. :thumbsup:

alex: I'll open a draft PR with the header fix and ndjson fallback. maria, want me to include a simple cli flag `--kv-trim`?

maria: yes please. let's gate kv trimming behind `--kv-trim` for now so we can gradually roll it.

ryan: I'll spike streaming upload today and post a minimal patch. if streaming is stable we can retire the multi-part buffer path.

sophia: I'll add a small sampling webhook for the dashboard so ops can mark specific runs to fully-retain or sample aggressively. helps for debugging vs cost.

maria: thanks all. created GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-runner/issues/719 with checklist and assigned tasks. will follow up in PRs. :eyes:
